description: Sabotages the integration tests of the public reader layer (tests/reader_real_writers/) must catch on their own, over files that child processes write. Run with tools/run-sabotage.ps1; see tools/README-sabotage.md for the format.

sabotages.name: a read starts one byte before the offset it was planned at
sabotages.why: Every file is delivered whole and in order under every option set, so a read that lands elsewhere repeats a byte or loses one.

sabotages.name: a chunk is the whole buffer rather than the bytes read
sabotages.why: The last read of a file is shorter than a buffer; its chunk then carries stale bytes past the end, and the range no longer matches the length.

sabotages.name: an entry the full client queue refused is dropped
sabotages.why: A client queue of two, and one nobody drains, are the cases where the queue refuses; the entry must wait and be delivered later, not be lost.

sabotages.name: the completion queue's size is not respected
sabotages.why: With a pool of sixty-four and a ring of sixteen it is the ring that limits the reads in flight; without the check the ring is asked for more than it holds.

sabotages.name: a size that is not a power of two is not refused
sabotages.why: The refusals are asserted through the public constructor, one cause at a time.

sabotages.name: a size below the least is accepted
sabotages.why: The ring would raise it, so the reader would run with a ring the caller did not ask for.

sabotages.name: a queue the allocator refuses is reported as a refused capacity
sabotages.why: The public constructor of the reader is where a caller meets the difference: a refused capacity is wrong on every machine, an allocation failure is this machine's answer and a smaller capacity may succeed. Asserted for both queues, at the capacity that used to abort and at the queue's largest.

sabotages.name: the text of an expect that cannot fail is changed
sabotages.why: Control: a change no test can observe. If this were caught, the manifest would be measuring something other than what these tests do.
